cards.explanation: The answer is that it's when the LORD brought them out of Egypt. Moses, Israel's leader, gives the reason in his own words: “…because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.” (Deuteronomy 16:1) So the month is a reminder of the day they walked out. You don't forget an anniversary like that, friends. Miss one and you'll hear about it for years.
The answer is False. Moses says the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt “by night.” (Deuteronomy 16:1) The Passover is tied to that night. Nothing in the verse says daylight.

The answer is in the place the LORD will choose. Moses says to offer the Passover sacrifice “…in the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name.” (Deuteronomy 16:2) Israel doesn't get to pick the spot. I bet some folks wanted the place with the best view. The LORD does the choosing, and Moses says it again in verse 6, like a man who really wants it to stick.

The word is haste. Moses says Israel left the land of Egypt “in haste.” (Deuteronomy 16:3) And he calls the unleavened bread “…the bread of affliction…” Haste is when you leave the house with one shoe on and figure out the rest later.

The word is remember. Moses says it's so “…that you may remember for the rest of your life the day you left the land of Egypt.” (Deuteronomy 16:3) The bread is there to help them remember. And he says for the rest of your life, so this isn't a one-year thing.

The answer is as much as the LORD has blessed them. The freewill offering is “…in proportion to how the LORD your God has blessed you…” (Deuteronomy 16:10) So the amount follows the blessing. It's not a fixed price tag.

The word is rejoice. Moses says, “…you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name…” (Deuteronomy 16:11) This feast is a joyful one. Moses is telling the whole guest list to celebrate.

The answer is False. Moses includes “…the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you.” in the list of people who rejoice before the LORD (Deuteronomy 16:11). He says it again for the Feast of Tabernacles (Deuteronomy 16:14). They're all invited.

The answer is True. Moses says, “Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and carefully follow these statutes.” (Deuteronomy 16:12) That's the memory he hands them, friends. And right with it comes the call to follow the statutes carefully.

The answer is after gathering from the threshing floor and winepress. Moses says to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days “…after you have gathered the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress.” (Deuteronomy 16:13) The gathering comes first and the feast follows. Hard work first, then the party.

The reason is that the LORD will bless their produce and work. Moses says, “…because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, so that your joy will be complete.” (Deuteronomy 16:15) Think about that: all the work of your hands, and the LORD is the one doing the blessing. I'd throw a seven-day feast for that too, and I'd bring the cookies.

The answer is all the men of Israel. Moses says, “…all your men are to appear before the LORD your God in the place He will choose…” (Deuteronomy 16:16) It's not a select few, friends. He says all your men, so the whole group goes.

The answer is False. Moses says, “No one should appear before the LORD empty-handed.” (Deuteronomy 16:16) Everybody brings a gift, and Moses says it's “…as he is able, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.” (Deuteronomy 16:17) The gift fits what each one has.
